title: Vasquez’s camp: venial against lesser precepts, not against those needful to charity
source_text: XXVIII. Qui vero docent peccatum veniale esse contra legem, & praeceptum aliquod, non autem solum praeter legem; distinguunt inter praecepta necessaria ad charitatem servandam, & salutem consequendam: & inter praecepta quae ad hoc utilia quidem sunt, sed non necessaria, & quorum violatio non impedit salutem. Et dicunt peccatum veniale non esse, sicut peccatum mortale, contra praeceptum aliquod necessarium ad salutem consequendam, & charitatem servandam, sed praeter illud. Verum propterea negari non debere peccatum veniale esse contra praeceptum aliquod, quod simpliciter praeceptum sit, licet non sit ex praeceptis praecipuis, & necessariis ad salutem. Ut videre est apud Gabr. Vasquez, modo citata Disputatione, cap. 3.
pass_a_gloss: But those who teach that venial sin is against the law and some precept, and not only beside the law, distinguish between precepts necessary for keeping charity and obtaining salvation, and precepts which are indeed useful for this but not necessary, and whose violation does not hinder salvation. And they say that venial sin is not, as mortal sin is, against some precept necessary for obtaining salvation and keeping charity, but beside that. Yet for that reason it ought not to be denied that venial sin is against some precept which is simply a precept, although it is not from the chief precepts and those necessary unto salvation. As may be seen in Gabriel Vázquez in the Disputation just cited, chapter 3.
pass_b_english: Vasquez’s side: venial is not against salvation-necessary precepts—yet still against some real, lesser precept.
So ‘beside’ the chief law need not mean ‘not against any precept at all.’
